patches_to_legacy: #5 chmod after copy in rearrange.py (defends against read-only master)
#6 inventory.py overflow detector now prefers layout defRPr over master bodyStyle
#7 replace.py text_frame.clear() gated on shape membership in replacements
#8 replace.py splits run text on \x0b and emits <a:br/> so soft line breaks survive serialization (no more _x000B_ literals)
#9 inventory.py no longer filters SLIDE_NUMBER placeholders; they are editable per Workflow A's contract
#10 replace.py auto-fills SLIDE_NUMBER placeholders with the slide's actual deck position when the JSON omits them
#11 replace.py overflow errors now name the placeholder_type and include a 30-char preview of the master text

brand.footer: Slalom. All Rights Reserved. Proprietary and Confidential.

body_slide_required_fills.DATE: deck year in brand.date_format (master DATE placeholder is ~0.28" wide; longer formats wrap or clip)
body_slide_required_fills.SLIDE_NUMBER: slide's actual deck position as plain text (master ships hardcoded; not a dynamic field)

slides.name: cover-basic
slides.when_to_use: Clean text-only deck opener with title + subtitle.

slides.name: cover-basic-alt
slides.when_to_use: Alternate basic cover. Use when the deck needs a second opener (back cover, section).

slides.name: cover-partner
slides.when_to_use: Opener co-branded with a partner (logo slot included). Use for joint-venture or alliance decks.

slides.name: cover-partner-alt
slides.when_to_use: Co-branded cover on white with a yellow accent stripe at left and partner-logo slot. Use when cover-partner's blue-heavy treatment feels too dense or formal — the white field reads as more open and consultative.

slides.name: cover-image
slides.when_to_use: Cover with a full-bleed image area on the right. The default master image is generic; swap via Workflow C if the photo doesn't match your context. Use when visuals set the tone and you want a custom photo, not stock.

slides.name: cover-image-2
slides.when_to_use: Image cover with a warm sunrise / mountain-silhouette photo. Use for nature, sustainability, journey, or new-beginning themes — the warm tone contrasts with the rest of the cover-image set, which is mostly cool blue.

slides.name: cover-image-3
slides.when_to_use: Image cover with a blue blurred-motion transit photo. Use for momentum, transformation, speed-of-change, or transit/logistics themes.

slides.name: cover-image-4
slides.when_to_use: Image cover with a blue circuit-board pattern. Use for technology, infrastructure, platform, or systems-engineering themes — pattern reads as 'large-scale, designed'.

slides.name: cover-image-5
slides.when_to_use: Image cover with a blue microchip / circuitry close-up. Use for hardware, semiconductors, low-level computing, or precision-engineering themes — closer crop than cover-image-4 reads as 'detail, expertise'.

slides.name: cover-image-6
slides.when_to_use: Image cover with a blue solar-panel / clean-energy pattern. Use for sustainability, clean-energy, ESG, or climate themes — the only cover-image variant with explicit renewable-energy imagery.

slides.name: partner-logo-lockup-1
slides.when_to_use: Partner logo lockup on a white field with a single partner column and a blue gradient accent. Use as a 'deck featuring partner X' opener when one alliance is the headline.

slides.name: partner-logo-lockup-2
slides.when_to_use: Partner logo lockup with a multi-partner grid (about a dozen logos) on a white-to-blue gradient. Use when the deck speaks to a portfolio of alliances rather than one named partner.

slides.name: partner-logo-lockup-3
slides.when_to_use: Partner logo lockup with a denser multi-partner grid in a more uniform layout. Use for industry-coalition or partner-program decks where the count of partners is the story.

slides.name: contents
slides.when_to_use: Table of contents. Lists chapters before diving in.

slides.name: contents-alt
slides.when_to_use: Numbered table-of-contents with right-aligned page numbers, book-style. Use when the deck has discrete numbered chapters and the audience needs an at-a-glance map; pick `contents` for a more visual TOC.

slides.name: agenda
slides.when_to_use: Meeting agenda with time-boxed items.

slides.name: agenda-summary
slides.when_to_use: 'Summarize your agenda' framing slide. Use when agenda is more narrative than time-boxed.

slides.name: overview
slides.when_to_use: Presentation overview with subheadline blocks. Primes the audience on what follows.

slides.name: our-understanding
slides.when_to_use: 'Our understanding' framing slide. Use to demonstrate you've heard the client's situation before pitching.

slides.name: together-intro
slides.when_to_use: 'Together, we've created great things' partnership intro. Use for established-client check-ins or extension pitches.

slides.name: team-intro
slides.when_to_use: Team introduction slide. Use to present the people on the call.

slides.name: team-intro-2
slides.when_to_use: Team-intro variant on a white field with light-blue accent (less ink than team-intro). Use when the headshots and bios are the focus and you want minimum visual competition from the slide chrome.

slides.name: team-intro-3
slides.when_to_use: Team-intro variant with a divided light/dark blue background. Use when the team has two distinct sub-groups (e.g., Slalom team + client team) that benefit from a visual split.

slides.name: section-divider
slides.when_to_use: Neutral section divider with a small intro-text block under the title. Use when the section break needs a one-line subtitle to set up what follows.

slides.name: section-divider-alt
slides.when_to_use: Full-bleed dark blue section divider with title only (no intro text). Use when you want maximum visual break and the section title speaks for itself.

slides.name: section-divider-color
slides.when_to_use: Full-bleed color divider in Slalom Blue (accent1). High-contrast visual reset. Pick this when the section is the headline color of the deck; pick a -color-N variant when the section maps to a different brand accent.

slides.name: section-divider-color-2
slides.when_to_use: Full-bleed color divider in Cyan (accent3). Use when the section's theme maps to cyan in your color story (often: data, tech, momentum).

slides.name: section-divider-color-3
slides.when_to_use: Full-bleed color divider in Coral Red (accent4). Use when the section's theme maps to coral red (often: risk, urgency, customer).

slides.name: section-divider-color-4
slides.when_to_use: Full-bleed color divider in Purple (accent5). Use when the section's theme maps to purple (often: people, culture, creative).

slides.name: section-divider-color-5
slides.when_to_use: Full-bleed color divider in Chartreuse (accent6). Use when the section's theme maps to chartreuse (often: growth, sustainability, energy).

slides.name: section-divider-numbered-1
slides.when_to_use: Numbered chapter divider 01 on a solid Slalom Blue background. Use as the first chapter of a long deck; the numbered series 1-5 is intended to be used in order, but the visual treatment varies (1-3 are solid colors, 4-5 are nature photos).

slides.name: section-divider-numbered-2
slides.when_to_use: Numbered chapter divider 02 with a cyan diagonal pattern. Use as chapter 2 in the numbered series — pairs with -1's solid blue.

slides.name: section-divider-numbered-3
slides.when_to_use: Numbered chapter divider 03 on a solid coral red background. Use as chapter 3 in the numbered series — high-contrast warm tone breaks up the cool-blue feel of -1 and -2.

slides.name: section-divider-numbered-4
slides.when_to_use: Numbered chapter divider 04 with a purple aerial-clouds photograph. Use as chapter 4 in the numbered series — visual treatment shifts from solid color to nature photography here.

slides.name: section-divider-numbered-5
slides.when_to_use: Numbered chapter divider 05 with a green farmland aerial photograph. Use as the final chapter (5) in the numbered series — completes the photo-pair with -4 for a closing nature beat.

slides.name: bio-card
slides.when_to_use: Single-person bio card with name, pronouns slot, and headshot area. Use for individual speaker intros.

slides.name: content-2col
slides.when_to_use: Two-column compare/contrast (Pros/Cons labels). Good for trade-off slides.

slides.name: content-3col
slides.when_to_use: Three-column layout for feature triads or parallel arguments.

slides.name: content-body
slides.when_to_use: Standard content slide with a title and rich body area (~5 sub-blocks).

slides.name: content-large
slides.when_to_use: Dense single-slide summary with 5 body panels. Use when packing a lot onto one page.

slides.name: table
slides.when_to_use: Plain table layout for tabular data. Use when you need rows-and-columns without the side-by-side comparison framing.

slides.name: comparison-table
slides.when_to_use: Comparison table layout. Use for feature-by-feature, vendor-by-vendor, or option matrices.

slides.name: pricing
slides.when_to_use: Pricing table for rate cards or plan tiers.

slides.name: cost-estimate
slides.when_to_use: Cost estimate with a team-structure breakdown. Use for staffing + cost proposals.

slides.name: at-a-glance
slides.when_to_use: Dense executive 'At a glance' one-pager with ~22 slots for stats, callouts, and metrics. Use as a high-density summary.

slides.name: short-headline
slides.when_to_use: Short-headline overview with two-line title + body. Use for terse 'state of X' summaries.

slides.name: chevron-4
slides.when_to_use: Four-step chevron with bullet list under each step. Real CHEVRON auto-shapes; sequential left-to-right flow with multi-line detail per step.

slides.name: bullets-4-cols
slides.when_to_use: Four-column bullets layout with horizontal divider bars at the top. Use for parallel multi-bullet content without implying sequential flow. (Not a chevron despite the master title 'Chevron process'.)

slides.name: process-visual
slides.when_to_use: Pipeline/intake flow with a TARGET endpoint (reactive intake -> pursuit -> engagement).

slides.name: gantt-chart
slides.when_to_use: Gantt chart with swim-lanes and go-live milestones. Use for multi-track delivery plans.

slides.name: timeline-weekly
slides.when_to_use: Weekly timeline (short horizon). Use for sprint or cadence plans.

slides.name: timeline-8week
slides.when_to_use: Eight-week timeline. Use for pilots or phase-0 engagements.

slides.name: timeline-quarterly
slides.when_to_use: Quarterly roadmap with sprints and releases. Use for quarter+ horizons.

slides.name: flowchart
slides.when_to_use: Branching flowchart with decision points. Use for approval trees or conditional logic.

slides.name: diagram-3-icons
slides.when_to_use: Hub-and-spoke with 3 icon-labeled concepts around a center. Use for 3-part frameworks.

slides.name: diagram-4-icons
slides.when_to_use: Hub-and-spoke with 4 icon-labeled concepts. Use for 4-quadrant or 4-pillar models.

slides.name: diagram-5-icons
slides.when_to_use: Hub-and-spoke with 5 icon-labeled concepts.

slides.name: diagram-6-icons
slides.when_to_use: Hub-and-spoke with 6 icons in a 3x2 grid around a central label. Strong choice for single-slide one-pagers with 6 items.

slides.name: venn-diagram
slides.when_to_use: Three-circle Venn showing overlap between 3 groups. Use for role or capability intersections.

slides.name: chart-bar
slides.when_to_use: Single-series bar graph. Use for ranked comparisons across categories.

slides.name: chart-bar-grouped
slides.when_to_use: Grouped bar graph (multiple labels per row). Use for multi-series ranked comparisons.

slides.name: chart-bar-multi
slides.when_to_use: Multi-series bar graph with several bars stacked horizontally per category. Use when you have 3+ series across a few categories (e.g., quarterly KPI trends across 4 metrics) — denser than chart-bar-grouped, less paired-comparison than chart-bar-comparison.

slides.name: chart-bar-comparison
slides.when_to_use: Side-by-side comparison bar graph. Use to contrast two or more groups directly.

slides.name: chart-pie
slides.when_to_use: Pie chart. Use for share-of-total at a glance (small N segments).

slides.name: chart-doughnut
slides.when_to_use: Doughnut chart. Modern alternative to a pie chart with center text space.

slides.name: chart-doughnut-comparison
slides.when_to_use: Three doughnut charts side-by-side with subheadlines under each. Use for before/middle/after share-of-total comparisons or three-scenario projections; pick chart-doughnut for a single ring with center text.

slides.name: chart-line
slides.when_to_use: Line graph. Use for time-series trends.

slides.name: chart-waterfall
slides.when_to_use: Waterfall chart. Use for cost build-ups, budget walks, or running totals.

slides.name: chart-stacked-column
slides.when_to_use: Stacked column graph. Use for parts-of-whole over multiple time periods or categories.

slides.name: device-frame-1
slides.when_to_use: Device frame layout 1 (image-to-be-replaced). Use for screenshots/mockups in a device shell. Body placeholder is 7.97" wide but the right ~1.5" sits behind the iPhone PICTURE shape (z-ordered above text); keep body copy under ~6.5" effective width or it disappears behind the device.

slides.name: device-frame-2
slides.when_to_use: Device frame layout 2. Same iPhone-overlay constraint as device-frame-1: keep body copy under ~6.5" effective width.

slides.name: device-frame-3
slides.when_to_use: Device frame layout 3. Same iPhone-overlay constraint as device-frame-1: keep body copy under ~6.5" effective width.

slides.name: device-frame-4
slides.when_to_use: Device frame layout 4. Same iPhone-overlay constraint as device-frame-1: keep body copy under ~6.5" effective width.

slides.name: storytelling-intro
slides.when_to_use: 'Storytelling Templates' section opener. Use to introduce a customer-outcome chapter.

slides.name: customer-outcome-1
slides.when_to_use: Customer-outcome storytelling layout 1. Headline highlights the outcome; supporting blocks for context, action, result.

slides.name: customer-outcome-2
slides.when_to_use: Customer-outcome layout with a customer quote as the hero. Photo right, headline + body left, large pull quote across the top. Use when a verbatim customer voice is the most compelling proof point.

slides.name: customer-outcome-3
slides.when_to_use: Customer-outcome layout with three sub-headline blocks pairing description and supporting detail. Photo left, structured body right. Use when the outcome has multiple dimensions (technology, scale, partners) you want to call out individually.

slides.name: customer-outcome-4
slides.when_to_use: Customer-outcome layout with an explicit Solutions / Cloud Provider stamp and supporting body. Photo left (people working), body right with stats and labeled solution callouts. Use when the cloud platform / technology vendor partnership is part of the outcome story.

slides.name: spro-cover
slides.when_to_use: Single Page Response Overview (SPRO) cover. Use as the opener for a one-page proposal response.

slides.name: spro-template
slides.when_to_use: SPRO content template. Use for the body of a one-page proposal.

slides.name: about-slalom-1
slides.when_to_use: About Slalom boilerplate slide 1. Use to introduce the firm to a new client.

slides.name: about-slalom-2
slides.when_to_use: About-Slalom boilerplate with one named partner column alongside the firm description. Use when introducing a deck co-authored or co-delivered with a single named partner.

slides.name: about-slalom-3
slides.when_to_use: About-Slalom boilerplate with two named partner columns alongside the firm description. Use for joint pitches involving two partners (e.g., Slalom + cloud provider + ISV).

slides.name: about-slalom-4
slides.when_to_use: About-Slalom boilerplate with three named partner columns. Use when the alliance / coalition itself is the narrative and three partners need equal billing alongside Slalom.

slides.name: quote
slides.when_to_use: Pull quote / testimonial slide. Use to spotlight a customer voice or strategic quote.

slides.name: quote-2
slides.when_to_use: Pull-quote on white with attribution above and a large blue headline-style quote below. Use for a short, high-impact quote (3-5 lines) where the words should dominate the slide.

slides.name: quote-3
slides.when_to_use: Pull-quote on white in body text size (smaller than quote-2) with attribution. Use when the quote is longer (multi-paragraph or 6+ lines) and won't fit at headline scale.

slides.name: quote-4
slides.when_to_use: Pull-quote on a Slalom Blue background with white text. Use for the closing quote of a section or deck — high-contrast color reset signals 'this is the takeaway'.

slides.name: closing-connect
slides.when_to_use: Closing slide listing 5 team contacts. Use as the last content page before copyright.

slides.name: thank-you-1
slides.when_to_use: Thank-you closer with a winding-road-through-forest stock photo. Use for journey or partnership-continuation themes; swap the photo via Workflow C if a road metaphor doesn't fit your context.

slides.name: thank-you-2
slides.when_to_use: Thank-you closer with a person looking out a car window through a landscape. Use for contemplation, perspective, or 'what's next' framings — more reflective tone than thank-you-1's road.

slides.name: thank-you-3
slides.when_to_use: Thank-you closer with a green winding road through hills (different angle from thank-you-1). Use when the road metaphor fits but you want a fresher, less corporate-stock feel.

slides.name: thank-you-4
slides.when_to_use: Thank-you closer with a person looking up / daydreaming portrait. Use for aspirational or future-looking closes — human-focused contrast to the landscape variants 1-3.

slides.name: thank-you-5
slides.when_to_use: Thank-you closer on a plain Slalom Blue background, text-only (no photo). Use when no stock imagery fits the deck context — fastest to brand-correct close, no Workflow C swap needed.

slides.name: copyright
slides.when_to_use: Copyright / disclaimer final slide. Use as the deck's last page.
